description: This bar chart, from the paper “The Unseen Targets of Hate — A Systematic Review of Hateful Communication Datasets,” illustrates the number of datasets published per year from 2012 to 2021, categorized by the primary language of the dataset. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10² (100), with major gridlines at 1, 10, and 100. The horizontal axis represents the year, spanning 2012 to 2021. Each year displays a grouped set of vertical bars, color-coded according to language: blue for English, orange for “All other,” green for Arabic, red for Bengali, purple for Spanish, and brown for Russian. English-language datasets consistently dominate across all years, with counts rising sharply from 1–2 in 2012–2015 to a peak of approximately 90 in 2021. “All other” languages also show strong growth, reaching about 40 datasets in 2020 and 2021. Arabic datasets appear from 2017 onward, peaking at around 15 in 2021. Spanish datasets emerge in 2017 and grow to about 10–12 by 2020–2021. Bengali and Russian datasets appear later (2018–2019) and remain relatively low, with Bengali peaking at ~5 in 2020 and Russian at ~8 in 2020. The chart visually emphasizes the overwhelming prevalence of English-language datasets and the gradual, but still limited, diversification into other languages over the decade.
